-800: Sparta, a Dorian state in the Eurotas valley.
c. 800: the Sabaean kingdom at Marib.
c. 800 BCE: the kingdom of Maha-Videha is founded under King Renu.
c. 800 BCE: the graveyard culture ends.
c. 800 BCE: the Dark Age ends and the age of the poleis begins.
800: Judah's western edge advances toward Lachish.

Cliopatria widens the shape at -800 by 222,552 km2 (west to 34.5 E, south to 31.2 N). Adad-nirari III "managed to defeat Aram-Damascus" (no year) and Shamshi-Adad V beat Marduk-balassu-iqbi in 813; the page dates no annexation.
800 BCE: the En Medio phase of the Oshara.
59,564 km2 for -800..-701: Humban-nikash I (743–717) 'supported Merodach-baladan against Sargon II'. The pages give no border; kept.
53,104 km2 for 800-751, bbox 41.30-46.11 E, 38.29-40.29 N, the Van basin and the Ararat plain.

Assyria as the dossier draws it (without Babylonia until 729), and without Carchemish and Sam'al, which paid no tribute and kept their own kings until 740/738 and are then tributaries that keep their land (m0800-m0701 events/2 and events/3)
Cliopatria's -800 shape cut to the Levant: the Phoenician coast from Arwad to the Carmel edge, valid -800..-751, without the western colonies

captions.text: 796 BCE (bridged): Hazael dies and the Israelite Transjordan contest ends.
c. 796 BC: Luhuti joins Hamath.

796 BCE (bridged): the contest ends with Hazael's reign (842–796); Israel's recovery followed Assyrian campaigns by Adad-nirari III (Samaria page) and Jeroboam II expanded the kingdom throughout northern Transjordan (793–753 or 786–746), no year.

793 BC: 'Established: 793 BC' (infobox; lead 'c. 8th century to 338 BC'). A league 'led by Alba Longa' of 'about 30 city-states and small settlements', 'created for protection against enemies from surrounding areas'; the eight names on Cato's inscription are Tusculum, Aricia, Lanuvium, Lavinium, Cora, Tibur, Pometia and Ardea.
782: Argishti I takes the Ararat plain and the Sevan side.
776: Duke Xiang holds Qian.
776: the Qin capital moves east from Quanqiu to Qian.
773 BC: Damascus pays tribute.
771: the Quanrong, invited by the Marquess of Shen, storm the Zhou capital.
771: the last dated mention of the Xianyun as a power.
771: the Quanrong sack Fenghao.
771: the capital moves east to Wangcheng (Luoyi).
771: the Eastern Zhou.
8th century BC: Zhongli arises in the Huai valley.
770: King Ping enfeoffs Duke Xiang and promises Qin 'the lands west of Qishan'.
770: Duke Wu moves Zheng east.
Cliopatria's 750 shape, used from 770 (years only)
769: Zheng conquers Kuai.
769: the state of Kuai ends in Zheng's conquest (list row).
769: Zheng annexes Hui (鄶). The SA states table: 'Hui (鄶 / 會 / 檜): 769 BCE, to Zheng'.
769: Zheng annexes Yan (鄢). The SA states table: 'Yan (鄢): 769 BCE, to Zheng'.
767: Zheng conquers Eastern Guo.
767: the state of Eastern Guo ends in Zheng's conquest (list row).
767: Zheng annexes Eastern Guo (東虢).
766: Duke Xiang of Qin dies fighting the Quanrong at Qishan.
763: Zheng conquers Hu (Luohe).
763: the state of Hu (Luohe) ends in Zheng's conquest (list row).
763: Zheng annexes Hu (胡). The SA states table: 'Hu (胡): 763 BCE, to Zheng'.
754: the Kushite Twenty-fifth Dynasty is established, with its reach at Thebes.
754 BC (bridged): the Kingdom of Arpad takes Aleppo.
753 BC: 'Founding of Rome: 753 BC' (infobox); Romulus the first king (753-716), who 'waged war with the Fidenates and Veientes and others'.
751: the vassal tint ends with Cliopatria's row.
751: the vassal tint ends with Cliopatria's row.
751: the vassal tint ends with Cliopatria's row.
751: the vassal tint ends with Cliopatria's row.
751: the vassal tint ends with Cliopatria's row.

751: Cliopatria's 'Zhou Dynasty' row ends; the state continues as the 'Later Zhou' row (eastern-zhou dossier) at Wangcheng 'until the Zhou were formally extinguished by the state of Qin in 256 BC'. The land of the fengjian states passes to their own dossiers (identity.successors).
8th century BC: Awsan arises at Wadi Markha.
770: the Zhou court moves east and the Eastern Zhou begins.
8th century BC: the kingdom of Dʿmt appears in Eritrea and northern Tigray.
c. 750 BC (bridged): the Assyrian tributary period ends 'in the middle of the 8th century'; the page gives no exact end, and Kustaspi is 'made to pay tribute to Sarduri II around 750 BCE'.
c. 750: Sarduri II's Euphrates gains, Melid and Kummuh, are tribute-paying land.
c. 750: the peak.
c. 750 BC: Kustaspi pays tribute to Sarduri II of Urartu ('around 750 BCE', page).
About 750: Qin holds Guanzhong.
750: Duke Wen of Qin breaks the Rong.
750: the Rong lose the Wei valley to Qin.
750: the Rong hold of the Wei valley ends, and with it this dossier.
750: Zheng annexes Ji (祭). The SA states table: 'Ji (祭): 750 BCE, to Zheng'.
Cai at Shangcai, 'enfeoffed at present-day Shangcai (lit.
'roughly the area of modern-day Dingtao County, Shandong Province', 'about 50 miles east of the point where the current course of the Yellow River changes from east to north-east'
Wanqiu, 'in present-day Huaiyang County in the plains of eastern Henan province'; 'At its peak, Chen encompassed fourteen cities in modern-day Henan and Anhui'
for 635-451: the royal domain without Henei and Yangfan, which King Xiang gave to Duke Wen of Jin; as drawn for 750-636
the shape without Laconia (Sparta's dossier) | unchanged between the corrected pieces of this Cliopatria shape

without the west bank of the Euphrates round Kummuh and Melid: the 743 BC battle was fought 'somewhere in Kummuh' and Tiglath-pileser III forced 'the Urartians back across the Euphrates'; Kummuh/Melid is an Urartian vassal tint only for 750-743 and Assyrian-held after
Lu as drawn, without the lands that were Ju's (Chu from 431) and Tan's (Yue from 414)

Qin as the page places it: the valley of Qin and Quanqiu in Gansu, Qian in Long County, 'the lands west of Qishan', 'its Guanzhong heartland', and the Shaanxi land west of the Yellow River that Wei conquered in 413-409; nothing east of the river
22,623 km2 around Shangqiu for -750..-488 (the shape runs to -481; 487-481 is the new keyframe song_-487).
Cliopatria's shape plus a 25 km circle round Tengzhou, valid -750..-298
7,027 km2 for -750..-551, the Zhaoge-Chuqiu-Diqiu plain north of the Yellow River.
the Xu heartland: Cliopatria's 750 shape plus Sihong and Pizhou, valid -750..-512
747: Corinth becomes a unified state under the Bacchiads.
746: a branch holds Quwo against the Jin marquises.

contests.war: Battle of Kummuh (Tiglath-Pileser III against Sarduri II's coalition)

captions.text: 743 BC: Tarhulara joins the anti-Assyrian alliance.
743 BC: Urartian hold on Kummuh broken.
743: Assyria strikes at Urartu's Euphrates bridgehead.
743: Urartu is pushed back across the Euphrates and loses Kummuh.
743: a single battle decides it; the page records no further fighting for the zone.
743 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III besieges Arpad.
743 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III defeats Gurgum.
740 BC: Arpad falls.
740 BC: Assyria annexes Arpad.
740 BC: the Kingdom of Arpad ends as an Assyrian province.
740 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Arpad.
740 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Arpad.
740 BC (campaign of 743-740): Tiglath-Pileser III installs Panamuwa II on the throne of Sam'al.
738 BC: Pisiri of Carchemish is a tributary of Tiglath-Pileser III.
738 BC: Assyria takes Luhuti.
738 BC: Hamath becomes an Assyrian tributary.
738 BC: Kustaspi is a tributary of Tiglath-Pileser III ('tributary to Tiglath-pileser III in 738 and 732 BCE', page).
738 BC: new provinces in Syria.
738 BC: Hama is left as a vassal.
738 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III annexes Pattin.
738 BC: Assyria annexes northern Phoenicia.
738 BC: Tyre and Byblos become Assyrian tributaries.
738 BC: Zabibe pays tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III (page); the Neo-Assyrian dossier has the Mu'na Arabs paying tribute after 734 but not Qedar.
c. 738: Tabal becomes a tributary of Assyria.
734 BC: Ammon pays tribute to Assyria.
734 BC: Edom pays tribute to Assyria.
734: Naxos and Syracuse founded.
734: Judah becomes an Assyrian tributary.
734 BC: Moab pays tribute to Assyria.
734 BC: Gaza falls and Assyria borders Egypt.
After 734 BC: "Asqaluna, Judah, Edom, Moab and Ammon, and the Mu’na Arab tribe, all began paying tribute."
734 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III's fifth Levant campaign reaches the Egyptian border.
733 BC: Syracuse 'founded by the Corinthians in 733 BC (according to the Thucydidean dating)'.
733 BC: Samsi rebels.
732: Tefnakht of Sais founds the Twenty-fourth Dynasty.
732 BCE: Tiglath-Pileser III annexes Aram.
732 BCE: the kingdom of Aram-Damascus ends with Rezin, its last king (754-732 BCE).
c. 732 BCE: Tiglath-Pileser III annexes Galilee and Gilead.
732 BCE: Israel is reduced to an Assyrian vassal kingdom.
732 BC: the tribute of Damascus ends in annexation (next event).
732 BC: Damascus falls.
732 BC: southern Israel becomes a vassal.
c. 732: Tefnakht of Sais breaks away.
Sais and the western Delta, with Memphis: the page says Bakenranef's authority was recognised in much of the Delta including Memphis
730: the court is at Tanis.
729 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon.
729 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III takes Babylon.
728: Piye of Kush takes Upper Egypt.
728: the Twenty-third Dynasty ends.
728: Piye marches on Egypt.
728: Piye holds Upper Egypt to Herakleopolis.
728: the Delta kings submit to Piye.
728: Piye sails south and goes home to Nubia, "never to return to Egypt" (Piye page); the fighting of his campaign ends and the Delta kings are left to rule.
728: Piye's army meets Tefnakht's coalition.
728: Tefnakht submits to Piye.
728: Piye returns to Nubia, "never to return to Egypt", leaving the Delta kings in place; the campaign ends.
728: Piye of Kush campaigns in Egypt.
Upper Egypt to Herakleopolis: the Piye page says his authority extended north only to Thebes, the western oases and Herakleopolis
724: the First Messenian War ends.
724: Messenia conquered; its people become helots.
Lacedaemon: Laconia and Messenia, whose people 'were enslaved after defeat' as helots, after the First Messenian War (743–724 BC)
722 BCE: Samaria falls.
722 BCE: the Kingdom of Israel ends.
722 BCE: the vassal kingdom ends with the fall of Samaria (722 in one passage of the Samaria page, c. 720 in others); Assyria turns it into a province in the loss below.
The 720s: Samaria falls.
The 720s: Samaria becomes an Assyrian province.
721-710 BC: Marduk-apla-iddina holds Babylon.
Early 721 BC: Marduk-apla-iddina seizes Babylon.
720: Achaeans and Troezenians found Sybaris.
c. 720 BC: the Yiqu Rong are first on record.
720: Magna Graecia.

-720: the dossier's gain 'the Achaean colonies of the Ionian coast of Italy' resolves the region 'Magna Graecia' (295 cells, the whole of southern Italy and Sicily) and so draws 279 cells to the aggregate for 11 years until the -709 keyframe drops them.
c. 720 BC: Yahu-Bihdi's revolt ends the tributary state.
c. 720 BC: Sargon II annexes Hamath.
c. 720 BC: the kingdom of Hamath ends under Sargon II. The Aramean displaced from Hamath formed part of the community 'in Egypt starting in 700 BCE' (Hamath page).
720 BC: Hama is annexed.
720 BC: Sargon II annexes Hama again after the battle of Qarqar on the Orontes.
719 BC: Assyria deposes Gunzinanu and sets up a vassal.
c. 718: Tabal is reorganised into Bit-Burutas.
717 BC: Sargon II ends the tributary state.
717 BC: Carchemish becomes an Assyrian province.
717 BC: the kingdom of Carchemish ends under Pisiri, its last king.
717 BC: Sargon II retakes Carchemish.
717 BC: Sargon II conquers Carchemish.
717 BC: the last Neo-Hittite kingdom falls.
717 BC: the tributary status ends with Sargon II's conquest of Carchemish ('conquered by Sargon II in 717 BC in the reign of King Pisiri'); the cells pass to Assyria in the loss below.
717 BC: Sargon II ends the kingdom.
717 BC: Sam'al passes to Assyria.
717 BC: the kingdom of Sam'al falls.
716 BC: Samsi gives Sargon II gifts.
716: the last campaign year of the Victory Stela (728-716).
716: the Twenty-second Dynasty ends.
715: Phrygia and Assyria come to blows.
714: Sargon II's campaign.
714: the campaign ends the same year; the page records no Assyrian annexation, and Cliopatria draws no change in the Urartu shape.
713 BC: Sargon II annexes Tabal.
713: the tribute ends in annexation.
713: Sargon II annexes Tabal.
713: the Tabal kingdom ends.
713: Zheng annexes Dai (戴). The SA states table: 'Dai (戴): 713 BCE, to Zheng'.
712 BC: Sargon II sacks Melid.
712 BC: Kammanu is annexed by Assyria.
712 BC: the city of Melid is handed to Kummuh.
712 BC: the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Kammanu ends (infobox 'disestablished 712 BC'); at the same time Cimmerians and Scythians invaded Anatolia and the city declined (Melid page).
712 BC: Muttallu is given the city of Melid.
712: Shebitku brings the whole Nile Valley under direct Kushite rule.
712: the Delta kings cease to be vassals when Shebitku takes the Delta directly (see the gain above).
712: the Kushite court moves its Egyptian capital to Memphis.
712: Shebitku ends the tributary status of Sais by conquering it.
712: Shebitku takes Sais and the Delta.
712: the dynasty ends with the death of Bakenranef.
the whole Nile Valley from the Delta to the south, which the 25th Dynasty page says Shebitku conquered "around 712 BC"
711 BC: Muwatalli III kills Tarhulara.
711 BC: Sargon II annexes Gurgum.
711 BC: Gurgum ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 711 BC', 'Succeeded by: Neo-Assyrian Empire').

-711: the Kush dossier's gain 'the Saite Delta' names the region 'Lower Egypt', which the gazetteer builds with the whole Matruh governorate, and its counterpart 'Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt (Sais)' is a name, not a slug, so the gain took 509 unowned desert cells (about 129,000 km2) as a detached Kushite exclave 1,000 km from Nubia.
711 BC: Sargon II captures Gath.
the 750 shape without Gath
710: the Achaeans found Croton.
710 BC: Sargon II retakes Babylon.
710 BC: Sargon II conquers Babylonia again.
709: Cyprus leaves the aggregate.
709 BC: Cyprus is absorbed.
709: Phrygia submits and a truce is struck.
708 BC: Sargon II invades.
708 BC: Kummuh becomes an Assyrian province.

708 BC: the kingdom of Kummuh ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 708 BC'). [Fixer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: region as above; confidence 3 lowered to 2: the year is the infobox's, the land is the researcher's reading.]
706: Spartans found Taras.
704: Huang first appears in the record, refusing Chu's summons.
704: Chu becomes a kingdom.
704: Quan annexed.
703 BC: Ba enters the record in the Hubei Han valley.
701: Sennacherib's campaign strips Judah.
701 BC: Sennacherib gives Judah's plundered lands to the Philistine kings.
